patch.value: Dynamic-read continuation cursors are born stale: pm health emits a cursor that its next invocation rejects

A default-budget full pm health read returns a valid-looking output continuation for the remaining checks, but an immediate retry with that cursor fails read_output_cursor_stale even though no tracker mutation occurred. Dynamic health fields such as telemetry timestamps make the collection fingerprint change between pages, so the token-efficient recovery path is unusable and the only successful workaround is an unbounded reread.

Dynamic read pagination binds every page to a stable snapshot or epoch whose identity survives volatile telemetry and clock fields; The exact emitted CLI recovery command succeeds without a tracker mutation and SDK and MCP cursor bindings behave identically; A deterministic regression advances health telemetry and clock fields between page one and page two while preserving the declared row collection; Cursor fingerprints include only collection identity and immutable query inputs or the producer freezes volatile inputs for the continuation lifetime; Stale cursors from genuine tracker or contract changes still fail closed with an executable restart command; Default-budget and unbounded reads are set-equivalent and do not duplicate or skip checks
Make every declared bounded-read continuation executable and snapshot-consistent across dynamic diagnostic surfaces
Agents can recover omitted health and diagnostic rows without discarding the first page or paying for an unbounded rerun
The complete ecosystem review exercised the recovery command exactly as emitted and it failed immediately on the current release
An output cursor returned by pm health resumes the exact declared check collection on the next invocation and returns the remaining rows with stable snapshot semantics.

pm health --check-only --full returned five of ten checks and a recovery cursor; the immediate retry returned read_output_cursor_stale. Re-running with --output-budget unbounded returned all ten checks successfully.
